Electronic configuration of scandium Sc(21) is:
\[ \text{Sc} = 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 4s^2 3d^1 \]
Here, s and d-orbitals are present at the outermost energy shell of scandium. Hence, group number of scandium will be = (2 + 1) = 3. So, position of scandium in periodic table is period-4 and group-3."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"What is the nature of aqueous solution of compound, formed by 'X' and 'Y' element? Explain with the bond formation of the compound.","marks":4,"answer":"X element mentioned in the stem is Hydrogen (H) and Y element is N. So, the compound formed by these two is NH₃. Aqueous solution of it is NH₄OH, which is a weak base. It partially dissociates to form NH₄⁺ and OH⁻ ions.
Bond formation technique of NH₃: Atomic number of Hydrogen is 1 and its electronic configuration—
\[ \text{H}(1) \longrightarrow 1s^1 \]
To achieve the stable electronic configuration of the nearest inert gas He, H requires 1 electron. On the other hand, electronic configuration of N, with atomic number 7 is—
\[ \text{N}(7) \longrightarrow 1s^2 2s^2 2p^3 \]
To achieve the stable electronic configuration, N atom has to either donate 5 electrons or receive 3 electrons. Since, N atom is unable to eject 5 electrons, it shares 3 electrons with three H atoms. Thus, three covalent bonds are formed and NH₃ is produced.
---"}]

In the case of CaCl₂, the Ca atom donates its two valence electrons to two Cl atoms and forms a Ca²⁺ ion, and attains the electronic configuration of the nearest inert gas Ar. parts:
[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is called molarity?","marks":1,"answer":"The amount of moles of a solute dissolved in per liter solution at a constant temperature is called molarity of that solution."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Write differences between organic and inorganic compounds.","marks":2,"answer":"The difference between organic and inorganic compound is given below:
Organic Compound:
i. Generally, organic compounds must have carbon. Example: Methane (CH₄)
ii. Usually, organic compounds take a long time to react.
iii. Organic compounds are generally formed by covalent bonding.
Inorganic Compound:
i. Except some exceptions, generally inorganic compounds have no carbon. Example: Hydrogen Sulphide (H₂S)
ii. Usually, inorganic compounds take lesser time to react.
iii. Inorganic compounds are usually formed by ionic or covalent bonding."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Why the ionization energy of ‘Y’ is more than that of ‘Z’ of the stem? Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"The energy that is required to transform an element into one mole positive ion removing one mole electron from its one mole atom in its gaseous state is called the ionization energy of that element. Based on the atomic mass, Z is Na and Y is Cl in the stem.
\[ \text{Na}(11) \rightarrow 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^1 \]
and \[ \text{Cl}(17) \rightarrow 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^5 \]
Since, both of these are located at the same period, their energy shell numbers are same. But chlorine has 6 more electrons and protons as well. Hence, the attraction force between the last orbital electrons and the nucleus of chlorine is greater than that of sodium. That’s why the energy required to remove an electron from chlorine atom is greater than that of Na atom. So we can say that, Cl has higher ionization potential than sodium (Na)."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Between compound XY₄ and ZY that is formed by the elements of the stem though one is water soluble but another is insoluble–Analyze.","marks":4,"answer":"Based on atomic mass, X, Y and Z in the stem mentioned above are C, Cl and Na respectively. So, XY₄ compound is CCl₄ and ZY compound is NaCl.
CCl₄ is a nonpolar covalent molecule. In CCl₄, each carbon atom is uniformly surrounded by four chlorine atoms. The electronegativity difference causes each C-Cl bond to be polar, but the symmetrical tetrahedral shape results in no net dipole moment. Thus CCl₄ is non-polar. Polar water molecules cannot attract nonpolar CCl₄, so it is insoluble.
NaCl is an ionic compound. In water, the polar water molecules attract the Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions, pulling them apart and dissolving the compound. Thus, NaCl is soluble in water.
---"}]

So, X is carbon (C). Carbon reacts with oxygen to form CO₂.
Electronic configuration:
\[ \text{C}(6) \rightarrow 1s^2 2s^2 2p^2 \]
\[ \text{O}(8) \rightarrow 1s^2 2s^2 2p^4 \]
Carbon has 4 valence electrons, oxygen has 6. To achieve octet, carbon shares 4 electrons with two oxygen atoms (double bonds). Each atom achieves 8 electrons in valence shell: C shares 4, each O shares 2 (plus 6 own). Thus, octet rule is followed."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Among elements of the stem, Ionization energy of the element 'Y' is the highest –Give reasons.","marks":4,"answer":"X, Y, Z are C, F, Mg.
Electronic configurations:
\[ \text{C} \rightarrow 1s^2 2s^2 2p^2 \ (\text{Period 2, Group 14}) \]
\[ \text{F} \rightarrow 1s^2 2s^2 2p^5 \ (\text{Period 2, Group 17}) \]
\[ \text{Mg} \rightarrow 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 \ (\text{Period 3, Group 2}) \]
Ionization energy increases across a period due to increasing nuclear charge and decreasing atomic size. F has the smallest atomic size in period 2 and highest effective nuclear charge, so it is hardest to remove an electron. Mg is in period 3, has larger size and lower ionization energy than period 2 elements. C has lower ionization energy than F because it is earlier in the period. Therefore, F has the highest ionization energy.
---"}]

subject: Chemistry
lesson: Radicals, Anions, Ionic Bonding, Octet vs Duet Rule
parts:
[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is called radical?","marks":1,"answer":"A bundle of atoms from more than one element combine together, receiving positive or negative charges and act as an ion of an element are called radicals."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"How does anion form?","marks":2,"answer":"After accepting electrons in their outermost shell, non-metals attain the stable electronic structure of the nearest inert gas and transform into negatively charged ions. These negatively charged ions are called anions. For example:
\[ \text{Cl} + e^- \rightarrow \text{Cl}^- \]
\[ \text{O} + 2e^- \rightarrow \text{O}^{2-} \]"},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain the bond formation process of molecule-(ii).","marks":3,"answer":"The molecule (ii) in the stem is CaCl₂.
Electron configurations of Ca and Cl are:
\[ \text{Ca}(20) \rightarrow 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 4s^2 \]
\[ \text{Cl}(17) \rightarrow 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^5 \]
Calcium has two electrons in its outermost shell. By donating these two electrons, Ca can attain the stable electron configuration of inert gas argon. On the other hand, Cl has 7 electrons in its outermost shell, and it needs one electron to attain the stable electronic configuration of inert gas argon. So, when calcium and chlorine react with each other, an atom of calcium donates two electrons and becomes calcium ion with two positive charges (Ca²⁺). Two chlorine atoms accept these two electrons to form two negatively charged chloride ions (Cl⁻). Positively charged calcium ion and negatively charged chloride ions are held by electrostatic attractive force that is called ionic bond."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Which of octet and duet rules is applicable to explain the bond formation of molecule-(i). Analyze with logic.","marks":4,"answer":"The molecule (i) is SO₃.
In SO₃, sulfur forms bonds with three oxygen atoms. The electronic configurations are:
\[ \text{S}(16) \rightarrow 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^4 \]
\[ \text{O}(8) \rightarrow 1s^2 2s^2 2p^4 \]
Sulfur has 6 valence electrons. In SO₃, sulfur forms three double bonds with three oxygen atoms, using all 6 of its valence electrons and sharing electrons from oxygen atoms. This results in sulfur having 12 electrons around it in its valence shell (expanded octet). Each oxygen atom achieves 8 electrons (octet).
Therefore, the oxygen atoms follow the octet rule (8 electrons each), but sulfur violates the octet rule by having 12 electrons (expanded octet). The duet rule applies only to hydrogen and helium (which are stable with 2 electrons), so it is not applicable to SO₃.
In conclusion: The oxygen atoms in SO₃ follow the octet rule, while sulfur exhibits an expanded octet (12 electrons), which is an exception to the octet rule. The duet rule is not applicable to this molecule.
---"}]

parts:
[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is Vaporisation?","marks":1,"answer":"The process of heating a liquid and turning it into gas is called evaporation or vaporization."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"What do you mean by kinetic theory of particle? Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"The attempt to explain the states of substances using intermolecular force of attraction and the kinetic energy of the particles is known as the kinetic theory of particles. When the particles inside a substance remain in very high force of attraction, they stay together and cannot move that much. This is the solid state. When heat is applied on such a solid substance, the particles start to vibrate. When more heat is applied, the particles lose some of their force of attraction and they start some movement. This state of matter is called a liquid. When more heat is applied on this liquid state of the substance, the particles receive the heat and the kinetic energy in them is increased. This kinetic energy is increased to a level where they lose intermolecular force of attraction almost completely and start to move freely. This is the gaseous state. When more heat is applied to this state of the substance, the particles will only increase their speed of movement."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain electric conductivity of 'Q'.","marks":3,"answer":"The element Q in the stem is Mg (atomic number 12).
The electronic configuration of Mg is:
\[ \text{Mg}(12) \rightarrow 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 \]
As there are 2 electrons in the valence shell of Mg, it is a metal. Metals conduct electricity due to delocalized electrons in the metallic lattice. In Mg, the valence electrons are free to move throughout the metal. When a potential difference is applied, these delocalized electrons drift towards the positive terminal, conducting electricity."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"An element of the stem gains the stability by more than one way —Analyze it.","marks":4,"answer":"The elements are: Q = Mg, R = Si, T = Cl.
The element T (Cl) gains stability by more than one way:
1. By accepting an electron to form Cl⁻ (ionic bond), e.g., in NaCl or MgCl₂.
2. By sharing an electron to form a covalent bond, e.g., in Cl₂ or HCl.
Thus, chlorine can achieve the stable octet of argon either by gaining an electron or by sharing electrons.
---"}]

For this, the activity of the acid is lost and the burning sensation of the wound stops."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain with diagram the bonding process of the compound formed by A and B elements.","marks":3,"answer":"The elements A and B are Li (period 2, group 1) and F (period 2, group 17). The compound is LiF.
Electronic configuration:
\[ \text{Li}(3) \rightarrow 1s^2 2s^1 \]
\[ \text{F}(9) \rightarrow 1s^2 2s^2 2p^5 \]
Li donates its one valence electron to achieve the configuration of He, becoming Li⁺. F accepts one electron to achieve the configuration of Ne, becoming F⁻. The electrostatic attraction between Li⁺ and F⁻ forms the ionic bond in LiF."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze the solubility of compound formed by C and D in polar solutions.","marks":4,"answer":"The elements C and D are P (period 3, group 15) and Cl (period 3, group 17). Compounds: PCl₃ and PCl₅.
Both are covalent compounds. PCl₃ is a polar molecule (trigonal pyramidal) and PCl₅ is nonpolar (trigonal bipyramidal). Generally, polar covalent compounds can dissolve in polar solvents like water if they can interact via dipole-dipole or ion-dipole forces. However, PCl₃ and PCl₅ react with water rather than simply dissolving:
\[ \text{PCl}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H}_3\text{PO}_3 + 3\text{HCl} \]
\[ \text{PCl}_5 + 4\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 + 5\text{HCl} \]
Thus, they are not simply soluble; they undergo hydrolysis.
---"}]

B has 3 valence electrons. It shares one electron with each of three Cl atoms, forming three covalent bonds. Each Cl atom achieves an octet (8 electrons in valence shell). However, B ends up with only 6 electrons in its valence shell (3 bonding pairs), which is less than the octet.
The term "duet rule" specifically refers to the stability achieved by having 2 electrons (as in H and He). For BCl₃, boron does not follow the duet rule; rather, it is an exception to the octet rule, being electron-deficient with only 6 electrons. The statement in the question appears to be incorrect or uses "duet rules" in a non-standard way to mean "electron pairs."

The bond formed between a metal and non-metal by donating and accepting electron thus creating a strong electrostatic force is ionic bond. The electronic configuration of S, Cl and Se are as follows:
S(16) = 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁴
Cl (17) = 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁵
Se (34) = 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3d¹⁰ 4s² 4p⁴
Group number and period number on the basis of their electronic configuration:
| Element | Group | Period |
|---------|-------|--------|
| S       | 16    | 3      |
| Cl      | 17    | 3      |
| Se      | 16    | 4      |
We know atomic size increases top to bottom in a group and decreases from left to right in a period. Atomic size is a periodic property. In a group the atomic size increases as a new energy shell is added after each period, thus the size increases. Again, due to the increase of electron number and proton number in the nucleus in a period, the attraction force between the electrons and the protons increase, thus the size decreases. As S and Cl is in the same period the size of S is greater than Cl and as Se is situated in the next period, so the size of Se is more than S. This makes the atomic size of Se the largest, then the atomic size of S in the middle and the atomic size of Cl is the smallest.

Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"Helium is placed in group 18 due to its inert nature. The electronic configuration of Helium is: He(2) → 1s². According to its configuration, it was supposed to be positioned in group 2. But the elements of group 2 are strongly electronegative. They are called alkaline earth metals. However, helium is an inert gas. Its properties are similar to other inert gases like, neon, argon, krypton, xenon, and radon. Moreover, its properties are not similar at all to those of the alkaline earth metals. Therefore, helium is placed with the other inert gases in group 18."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Describe the bond formation process by the elements B and C of the stem with diagram.","marks":3,"answer":"From the stem we can say that, the element B and C are magnesium (Mg) and chlorine (Cl) respectively. Mg is a metallic element and Cl is a non-metal element. Therefore, the chemical bond formed between Mg and Cl will be ionic or electrovalent bond. Ionic bonds are formed by exchanging electrons between two compounds. The electron configurations of Mg and Cl are:
Mg (12) → 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s²
Cl (17) → 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁵
Here, Mg donates two electrons from its outermost energy level and forms Mg²⁺ cation. On the other hand, 2 Cl molecules accepts one electron each, donated by Mg and becomes two Cl⁻ anion. These two mutually opposite charges are attracted towards each other and forms ionic bond. The diagram of their bond formation is given below:"},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Although the compound formed by A and C does not follow octet rule but the compound formed by B and C follows octet rule—Analyze.","marks":4,"answer":"From the stem we can say that, the element A, B, and C are boron(B), magnesium (Mg), and chlorine (Cl) respectively. All elements tend to make the electronic configuration of inert gases at their outermost energy level. All inert gases other than helium have 8 electrons at their outermost energy level. When constituting a molecule, an element obtains the electronic configuration of inert gases, holding electrons by means of donating, accepting, or sharing electrons. This is knows as the octet rule. The compound formed by A and C is BCl₃ (boron trichloride) and the compound formed by B and Cl is MgCl₂ (magnesium chloride). BCl₃ does not follow the octet rule. The electron configuration of B and Cl are as follows:
B (5) → 1s² 2s² 2p¹
Cl (17) → 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁵
As we can see, B has three electrons in its outermost energy level. So, to achieve octet, boron needs to either donate these three electrons or to accept 5 electrons. In BCl₃, boron shares its three electrons with three chlorine molecules, each in need of one electron. So, each Cl molecules managed to have their octet filled, however, boron still needs more electrons to fill its octet, having only 6 electrons after sharing. So, BCl₃ fails to obey the octet rule. In the compound MgCl₂, we see that, Mg needs to donate two electrons to achieve octet, which it does, and forms Mg²⁺ ion. These two electrons are accepted by two Cl molecules to become Cl⁻ ions. Since they are opposite in charge, they are attracted to each other and ionic bond is formed to make MgCl₂. Therefore, we can say that, BCl₃ does not follow the octet rule but MgCl₂ does.
---"}]

The resulting compound XY₃ is BF₃ (NOT XY) and it is formed by covalent bond. This compound does not follow the Octet rule.
Clarification on "Duet Rule": The duet rule specifically states that hydrogen and helium are stable with 2 electrons in their valence shell. BF₃ does NOT follow the duet rule in the traditional sense.
In BF₃:
- Each F atom achieves an octet (8 electrons) by sharing one electron with B and having 3 lone pairs (6 electrons)
- B atom has only 6 electrons in its valence shell (3 bonding pairs), which is an incomplete octet
- B is electron-deficient
The statement "follows duet rule" because it has "3 pairs or 6 electrons" is a misuse of terminology. Having electron pairs does not constitute following the "duet rule." The duet rule is specifically about having 2 total electrons (as in H₂ or He).
Corrected explanation: BF₃ is an exception to the octet rule. Boron has only 6 electrons (3 bonding pairs) in its valence shell, making it electron-deficient. It does not follow the octet rule, and the duet rule (2 electrons total) is not applicable to this molecule. BF₃ is stable despite the incomplete octet due to the strong B-F covalent bonds."}]
